questions.topic: eGurukul · Gas Exchange - V Q Ratio
questions.stem: A patient with congestive heart failure, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea is referred for pulmonary function testing in the supine and upright positions. Which of the following is higher at the apex of the lung than at the base when a person is upright?
questions.solutionHtml:
V/Q ratio
  • When a person is upright, blood flow is higher at the base of the lung due to the effect of gravity. Ventilation, or the amount of air that reaches the alveoli, is also higher at the base of the lung due to increased compliance and decreased resistance in the lower airways.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.643–644, 662–663, 686–688.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Gas Exchange - V Q Ratio
questions.stem: A healthy 26-year-old woman undergoes pulmonary exercise stress testing prior to starting a training regimen in preparation for her first marathon. Normally, during moderate aerobic exercise, which of the following occurs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alveolar ventilation increases
  • During moderate aerobic exercise, oxygen consumption and CO2 production increase, and alveolar ventilation increases in proportion.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1247

questions.topic: eGurukul · Gas Exchange - V Q Ratio
questions.solutionHtml:
Apex of lung
  • Ventilation-perfusion ratio (V/Q ratio) is the ratio of the amount of air reaching the alveoli (ventilation) to the amount of blood perfusing the alveoli (perfusion). The V/Q ratio is not uniform throughout the lung, and it varies from the apex (top) to the base (bottom) of the lung.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 603
